author: difficulty53_b3

source_artifacts.claim: The resolved campaign order places level_45 at position 6, after the five prior rooms.
The room defines its subtitle, spawn layout, static dock and tissue platforms, a powered moving lift, the safe floor, the Pac-only hold pad, and both matching exits.
The room starts Gem's bubble and Cana's boomerang after the Pac lift pad activates; no collectible or physical hazard is authored.
A hold pad is active only while an accepted hero occupies it; its power effect supplies power to the moving lift.
Moving platforms advance only when active, motorized, and powered; bodies standing on them are carried, while a colliding rider can stop movement.
The physics update applies jump/movement input, resolves contacts with other bodies, and applies the Float velocity while the effect is active.
Player contact can push a villain body by transferring the player's horizontal velocity, supporting Gem as a movable step.
Villain bodies move under gravity and settle against solids; acid or falling below the world causes a timed absence and return home.
A bubble hit gives Isp Float for 1.4 seconds and Pac Sticky; a boomerang gives Isp Dizzy or Pac Shove, with temporary effects and immunity.
Attacks attached to the lift pad begin when that pad becomes active.
Projectiles apply their temporary player effects on collision; a bubble can affect either player and a descending Pac may instead bounce from its top.
Position 2 introduced a powered lift, an Isp-controlled door, a shared restore pad, and exits for both heroes.
Position 1 introduced both-exit completion and a held Isp pad that lets Pac cross to a rescue pad.
Position 4 uses an Isp-held motor stop while Pac crosses a ferry route to rescue; it also includes a dangerous slime pond and recovery folds.
Position 3 explicitly assigns Pac to hold STEADY while Isp crosses to RESCUE.
Position 5 teaches a partner launch and return-pad lesson; that recoil mechanic is not used in this room.

prior_knowledge.concept: Both matching exits are the completion goal.

evidence.claim: The first campaign room is titled Hold That Door! and frames completion as nobody being left behind; both hero exits are defined at lines 150-153.
The first capture visibly labels separate ISP and PAC exits and the subtitle Nobody gets left behind.

prior_knowledge.concept: One hero can hold a pad while the partner crosses to a distinct route or rescue point.

evidence.claim: The fourth campaign room assigns Pac to hold STEADY while Isp reaches RESCUE, then extends rescue behavior to Pac's path.
The fourth room visibly states Pac holds STEADY until Isp reaches RESCUE.

prior_knowledge.concept: A moving lift can carry a hero, can require power, and can be missed and reboarded.

evidence.claim: The second campaign room has a powered moving lift and a restore pad that powers it when both heroes occupy it.
The second room visibly shows the lift, the two-cell restore cue, and a jump-from-left / wait-at-the-side reminder.

prior_knowledge.concept: A partner-controlled stop or steady pad can make a route usable while the other hero advances.

evidence.claim: The third campaign room gives Isp a held STOP pad controlling the ferry and Pac a rescue pad beyond it.
The third room visibly labels ISP STOP, a ferry, and the far-side rescue route.

prior_knowledge.concept: Bubble Float can change a route or interrupt a ride; this is an earlier lesson that can be reused as an alternate path.

evidence.claim: The third campaign room includes Gem's bubble and explicitly describes floating Isp away from the ferry brake.
Gem's visible dialogue says Float away from that ferry brake!

mechanics.fact: Isp spawns on the high fold next to pushable Gem; Pac spawns on the shared dock. Gem's body can be pushed by horizontal player contact and will fall onto the dock, where it can act as a step to reach the middle tissue.

evidence.claim: Gem is placed on the high fold at the left while Cana is near the lower return path.
Player contact transfers horizontal velocity to an active villain body.
The shared dock sits below the high fold and the raised Pac middle tissue.

mechanics.fact: The powered lift begins at the shared dock and moves vertically by 184 pixels on a 7-second cycle; it only moves when powered. Pac alone is accepted on HOLD LIFT, which is a hold pad requiring one unit of weight and supplies power to the lift while occupied.

evidence.claim: The powered lift and the Pac-only hold pad with its power effect are defined here.
A moving platform marked requiresPower has no power until an active pad supplies it.
Pad occupancy activates a hold pad and applies its power effect.

mechanics.fact: A body standing on a powered moving platform is carried with it; if the lift is already away from the dock, its repeating motion allows the pair to wait for its return and try boarding again.

evidence.claim: Powered moving platforms move and carry supported bodies.
The lift moves through a repeated 7-second vertical cycle.
The authored route describes waiting on the dock while Pac keeps HOLD LIFT active until the lift returns; this text is not counted as a visible player cue because the optional hint remained closed.

mechanics.fact: The primary mandatory route is a sequential handoff: Isp moves Gem down to the dock; Pac uses Gem as a step to reach and hold HOLD LIFT; Isp boards the lift and rides up; Pac releases the pad and returns across the lower safe path; both reach their matching exits.

evidence.claim: The authored route names the Gem step, Pac pad, Isp ride, and Pac lower return.
The accepted ordinary-input route for position 6 records movement and jumps from both control sets and is sourced from an accepted browser clear case.
During the wait, Isp's y position rises from 427.77 to 322.63 while Pac remains at x608.25,y374 on the hold area, consistent with the lift carrying Isp while Pac supplies power.
The accepted attempt ends with both players at their matching exits and phase complete.

mechanics.fact: The level defines no collectibles and no physical hazards; a full-width safe floor lies below the route. Pac's hold pad also starts Gem's bubble and Cana's boomerang. A hit can impose brief Float, Sticky, Dizzy, or Shove effects, but the authored level has no lethal hazard for these effects to push a hero into.

evidence.claim: A full-width safe floor and both exits are present; the hazards and collectibles arrays are empty.
The two temporary attacks start when Pac occupies HOLD LIFT.
Float, Sticky, Dizzy, and Shove have short defined effect durations.
Projectile hits apply the brief movement effects to players.

legal_routes.name: Powered lift handoff with separate exits

steps.goal: Open the shared dock by moving Gem off the high fold.
steps.action: Move across the upper fold into Gem and nudge him down to the dock; use the moved Gem as a step for Pac.
steps.expected_feedback: Gem should move under horizontal contact and settle on the lower dock; Pac can then jump from the dock/Gem to the middle tissue.
steps.observed_feedback: The ordinary-input trace records Isp moving right and then left to the dock before Pac's climb. The replay does not record Gem coordinates, so the exact displacement is supported by the authored physics/route, not directly observed in the route log.

evidence.claim: Gem starts on the high fold and the authored route calls for nudging him down.
Horizontal player contact can push the villain body.
After the first rightward movement, Isp has reached the shared-dock region.

steps.goal: Reach HOLD LIFT while Isp prepares to board.
steps.action: Jump from the lower dock, using Gem as an intermediate step if needed, then settle on the Pac-only hold pad on the middle tissue.
steps.expected_feedback: The pad should become active while Pac overlaps it and supply lift power; the powered lift can then carry a supported Isp upward.
steps.observed_feedback: The accepted trace moves Pac from the lower dock to x608.25,y374 and keeps Pac there while Isp ascends; the state log does not expose pad occupancy directly.

evidence.claim: Only Pac can activate HOLD LIFT; occupying the pad powers the lift.
Pac reaches the pad region at x608.25,y374 while Isp approaches the lift.

steps.goal: Ride the powered lift to the upper-right route.
steps.action: Board the lift from the shared dock and stay aboard while Pac keeps HOLD LIFT active; leave for the upper-right tissue when it is within reach.
steps.expected_feedback: The platform should carry Isp upward while it is powered; the upper-right platform leads to the matching ISP exit.
steps.observed_feedback: Across the ordinary-input wait, Isp rises from y427.77 to y322.63 while Pac stays at x608.25,y374; the final state places Isp at x1070,y274 in the ISP exit with the level complete.

evidence.claim: Moving platforms carry bodies standing on them.
Isp rises while Pac remains at the hold position.
Isp reaches the upper-right exit area while Pac starts the lower return.

steps.goal: Return from the hold pad to the lower-left PAC exit.
steps.action: Release HOLD LIFT after Isp can complete the upper route, descend to the safe floor/dock, and traverse left to the orange exit.
steps.expected_feedback: The lift stops when it loses power; Pac can leave the control and use the lower route to the matching exit.
steps.observed_feedback: The route records Pac leaving the hold area and moving left while Isp remains at the upper exit; the attempt completes with Pac at x83.68,y458 and zero retries.

evidence.claim: The lower region has a continuous safe floor and the PAC exit is at lower left.
The accepted input route completes at the PAC exit with zero retries.
The room's accepted ordinary-input route uses both control sets and is an accepted built-browser complete case.
The only recorded attempt has zero retries.

legal_routes.name: Gem FLOAT shortcut to the upper route

steps.goal: Start the pad-bound attacks and give Isp time to receive Gem's bubble.
steps.action: Reach and hold HOLD LIFT as in the powered route, while Isp stays in the bubble's target area near the lower lift approach.
steps.expected_feedback: The active pad starts Gem's bubble attack; a bubble hit to Isp applies FLOAT for 1.4 seconds, allowing upward movement without relying on the powered lift for the whole ascent.
steps.observed_feedback: This legal shortcut is supported by the authored attack target and movement rules but was not replayed in the supplied journey; the route log documents only the powered-lift clear.

evidence.claim: Gem's bubble begins when Pac activates HOLD LIFT and targets the lower lift approach.
A bubble hit gives Isp a temporary Float effect.
Float prevents ordinary jump triggering while active.
While floating, Isp rises at a steady vertical velocity.

steps.goal: Use Float to reach the upper-right route and matching exit.
steps.action: Steer horizontally during the Float window to land on the upper-right tissue and continue to the ISP exit; Pac can leave the pad when Isp no longer needs another powered ride.
steps.expected_feedback: If the bubble reaches Isp near the lower approach, the short upward drift may substitute for riding the lift to the upper ledge; Pac still uses the lower path to the PAC exit.
steps.observed_feedback: This alternative's full geometry has not been replayed in the supplied evidence; treat route feasibility as source-inferred, not replay-proven.

evidence.claim: An upper-right tissue platform connects to Isp's matching exit, and a safe floor remains below.
Float imposes upward velocity for the effect duration, while ordinary gravity is suspended.
Gem's bubble is a second attack tied to the same Pac pad and targets the lift approach.
The bubble grants Isp Float when it hits.

isp: Pushes Gem from the high fold toward the dock to make a step accessible to Pac.
Boards and rides the powered lift while Pac holds the control, then takes the upper-right exit.
Can potentially use Gem's pad-started bubble for a Float shortcut to the upper route; this path is source-inferred and not replayed here.
pac: Climbs from the dock via Gem to the middle tissue and occupies the Pac-only HOLD LIFT pad.
Keeps the lift powered long enough for Isp to board and ascend, then releases the pad and returns along the lower route to the PAC exit.
If the lift has passed the dock, can wait on HOLD LIFT while Isp waits at the dock for a return; this contingency is source-inferred rather than replayed.

common_mistakes.mistake: Isp or Pac reaches the lift after it has already left the dock, or Isp misses the moving platform.
common_mistakes.consequence: The pair loses the immediate boarding opportunity and may have to wait through another lift cycle; this is delay and repeated traversal, not a death reset.
common_mistakes.recovery: Keep Pac on HOLD LIFT so the platform remains powered; Isp waits on the shared dock and boards when the lift returns. The source describes this recovery, but the supplied journey did not replay a missed-lift failure.

evidence.claim: The authored route gives a wait-for-return recovery for a missed boarding opportunity.
The lift is cyclic and requires the Pac hold pad for power.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac leaves HOLD LIFT before Isp is safely able to finish the upper route.
common_mistakes.consequence: The lift loses power and stops, potentially stranding Isp on the platform or below the upper tissue.
common_mistakes.recovery: Pac can return to the pad to supply power again; Isp can wait for a powered cycle or descend to the safe floor and retry. This recovery is inferred from pad and platform logic, not replayed.

evidence.claim: The power effect is present only while the hold pad remains occupied.
An unpowered moving platform stops and carries riders only while moving.
The full-width floor below is a safe surface for a retry.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac or Isp is hit by Cana's boomerang while the lift pad is active.
common_mistakes.consequence: Pac may be shoved and Isp may be dizzy briefly, interrupting pad occupancy or movement; the effect is temporary and the room has a safe floor, so the likely cost is losing position or waiting for another lift cycle.
common_mistakes.recovery: Return to the pad and board again after the lift returns if needed. The accepted journey clear did not record a hit or retries; this recovery is source-inferred.

evidence.claim: Cana's boomerang starts from Pac's lift pad.
A boomerang hit gives Pac Shove or Isp Dizzy for a short duration.

reasoning.rationale: Players must connect pushing Gem to the raised middle tissue, holding Pac's pad to power the lift, and splitting to the two exits. The sequence is causal but linear; the alternative Float route does not make the powered lift mandatory.

evidence.claim: The subtitle and level geometry encode the step, held lift, and two-role sequence.
An ordinary-input attempt completed both exits without retries.

cooperation.rationale: The main route has distinct roles and a handoff: Pac must maintain power while Isp rides, then Pac returns to the lower exit. This matches the rubric's distinct-role/one-handoff anchor; it does not require repeated simultaneous coordination.

evidence.claim: Only Pac can keep the lift powered while Isp boards and rides.
The ordinary-input route keeps Pac at the pad while Isp rides upward.

execution.rationale: Several jumps and placements are needed to get Pac to the pad, board Isp, and route both heroes to separate exits. The accepted route shows these inputs are feasible but does not measure human precision or effort.

evidence.claim: The accepted complete route uses several movement and jump intervals from both control sets.
Platforms and exits are separated vertically and horizontally, requiring traversal and boarding.

timing.rationale: The powered lift cycles continuously on a 7-second period, creating a boarding choice, but the repeatable cycle and authored wait-at-the-dock recovery avoid a narrow one-shot window.

evidence.claim: The lift repeats its vertical movement on a 7-second cycle.
The authored route explicitly permits waiting for the lift's return.

hazards.rationale: No physical hazards or collectibles are authored, and a full-width safe floor sits below the platforms. Pad-triggered attacks can cause brief movement interference, but this room gives those effects no lethal surface to push a hero into; they can cost position and time instead.

evidence.claim: The level has a full-width safe floor and an empty hazards array.
The attacks are tied to the hold pad rather than being permanent physical hazards.
All relevant attack effects are temporary.

novelty.rationale: A powered lift was introduced in position 2, and held-pad teamwork across a route was practiced in positions 1, 3, and 4. This room recombines those familiar ideas into a Pac-powered boarding handoff plus a separate lower return; the exact combination is new, while the underlying lift and cooperative-pad model is not.

evidence.claim: Position 2 introduced a powered lift and two-hero power/restore interaction.
Position 3 introduced Pac holding a route open while Isp reaches rescue.
The new combination has Pac hold power for an Isp passenger on a cycling lift.

recovery_cost.rationale: Missing the lift or falling from an intermediate ledge does not require a full reset: the lift returns, Pac can keep the power pad active, and the continuous floor allows repositioning. Some approach and waiting may need repeating. This is source-inferred recovery; the supplied clear route had no retries and did not exercise a failure.

evidence.claim: The lift repeats and the safe floor spans the room.
The source describes waiting on the dock for the lift to return.
The accepted route records zero retries, so it proves the clear but not the recovery case.

solution_clarity.rationale: The subtitle says to make a step, share the lift, and split the route; the canvas labels PAC HOLD LIFT and dialogue points at Gem. These cues suggest the roles, but learners still need to infer that Gem can be pushed into a step and that Pac should keep the pad active until Isp has boarded.

evidence.claim: The screenshot visibly shows the PAC HOLD LIFT label, Gem next to Isp, and the subtitle about a step and shared lift.
The room's actual step, hold-pad, moving-lift, and route roles are explicit in authored mechanics, while the optional route hint is separate from the closed first-pass hint.

control_friction.rationale: The accepted automation trace shows a valid clear but does not measure keyboard reliability, rollover, or simultaneous-input friction for two humans. Those control properties remain unknown.

evidence.claim: The route records key intervals and a clear outcome, but no dedicated test of human keyboard reliability or two-person input friction.

confidence_reason: Authored mechanics and an accepted ordinary-input clear jointly establish a legal route, its cooperative roles, the moving lift, and safe recovery surfaces. Human novice difficulty, control friction, the exact Gem motion in the replay, the Float shortcut's full geometry, and failures/recovery were not directly observed.

confirmed: The two distant matching exits and split-route goal are correct; the ordinary route completes both.
The PAC-labeled middle pad is central to Isp's upper route: Pac occupies HOLD LIFT while Isp rides upward.
The ordinary route separates Isp's upper exit from Pac's lower return.
missed_mechanics: The critical earlier step is moving pushable Gem down from the high fold so Pac can reach the raised middle tissue.
The lift cycles vertically every 7 seconds and can be missed without a reset; Pac can remain on the hold pad while Isp waits for the return.
Occupying the lift pad also starts Gem's bubble and Cana's boomerang attacks; Gem's bubble can provide a Float shortcut for Isp.
The lower full-width floor is safe, the level has no authored physical hazards or collectibles, and both exits are mandatory.
incorrect_inferences: The first pass speculated that the bubble or boomerang might be mandatory. The primary ordinary-input clear uses the powered lift, and source rules make the attacks optional side effects; the bubble Float shortcut is legal but not required.
The first pass left lift activation and control reliability unclear. Source confirms the hold pad powers the lift; control reliability remains untested and is still unknown.
changed_judgments: Timing changed from unknown to 1 because the lift creates a boarding choice on a repeatable 7-second cycle, with a safe wait-for-return route rather than a narrow window.

Hazards changed from unknown to 0 because the authored hazard list is empty and a full-width safe floor catches falls; temporary interference can disrupt position but does not create a lethal route hazard here.
Novelty is kept at 2 but reinterpreted: the lift and partner-held-pad concepts were introduced earlier, and this room combines them in a new boarding handoff and split return.
Recovery cost changed from unknown to 1 because the lift returns and the lower floor permits repositioning; this recovery is inferred from source and was not exercised by the zero-retry route.
Solution clarity changed from 3 to 2 after reading the visible step/lift subtitle and PAC HOLD LIFT cue together; the Gem step and required hold duration still require a causal test.
unresolved: No human novice has played the room, so actual comprehension, time, frustration, enjoyment, or success rate remain unknown.
The ordinary journey does not log Gem's body position, so its push into the dock is source-supported but not replay-proven.
The supplied ordinary route does not exercise the missed-lift or projectile-hit recovery cases, and the complete Gem Float shortcut was not replayed.
The route trace does not establish two-human keyboard reliability or shared-keyboard control friction.

single_operator_note: One operator would have to alternate attention between holding Pac on HOLD LIFT and steering Isp onto and along the lift, then return Pac to the lower exit. This likely adds coordination demand; keyboard rollover and simultaneous-input behavior were not tested.
